name: hcapp
description: Read HCAPP data and create tasks and comments within your bot permissions.

interface.longDescription: Explore HCAPP forms, filter tasks, compute counts, sums and averages grouped by user, step, field or period in one call, see where a vehicle is and how far it has to go when a telematics integration is opened to bots, summarize fields and comments, and create tasks and comments when requested. Sign in to HCAPP as an admin or super-admin, choose an active bot from your company, and approve access. No manual Bot-token entry is needed. Reading and creation require their respective OAuth scopes and bot permissions. Access lasts up to 8 hours; reconnect to renew it. Creation uses Bot API limits and may send its standard notifications. Updating and deleting are unavailable. Bot access is determined by company, granted forms and action rights. Human task-level permissions do not restrict bots. An HCAPP administrator account with a configured bot and a valid server-side Bot API token is required. Inspect basic form details and map task user IDs to names through the company user directory. Form-user lookup includes basic form access rights; email and phone are opt-in. Use resolved IDs for assignees and comment recipients.

positive.description: Discover forms and form-user identities. Fixture: the demo bot has access to the Orders, Tasks and Vehicles forms, and Orders has active demo users.
positive.prompt: Show my available HCAPP forms, then show the Orders form details and users who can be responsible for its tasks. Do not include contact details.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve Orders from returned forms. Return its actual ID, bot rights and responsible-user requirement. Follow form-user cursors and return actual user IDs and names with can_be_responsible=true. Do not request contacts, disclose private access conditions or include users from another company.

positive.description: Aggregate instead of paging. Fixture: Orders has a numeric Freight field, a Truck plates link field and several orders this month.
positive.prompt: In the Orders form, how many orders per truck this month, and what is the total Freight this month?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the form, the Truck plates field and the Freight field IDs, then call aggregate_tasks once with count grouped by the truck field and sum of Freight over the current month. Report totals from the response and the timezone used; do not page through list_tasks to count.

positive.description: Vehicle position and remaining route. Fixture: a Mapon integration opened to bots with a Google key, truck 010BTN, and order DEMO-2026-001 (Helsinki to Hamburg) with a Vehicle location field.
positive.prompt: Where is truck 010BTN now and how many kilometres are left on its order DEMO-2026-001?
positive.expected_behavior: List fleet integrations, call get_vehicle_status with the plate and report the address, speed and how old the position is. Resolve order DEMO-2026-001 and call get_route_progress with its task_id; report remaining km, next stop and ETA, noting that figures are car routing. Do not invent coordinates or distances.

positive.description: Read a task, post a summary comment and give attachment links. Fixture: order DEMO-2026-001 (Helsinki to Hamburg, truck 010BTN) has at least one comment and two attached PDFs, one named mock_CMR_DEMO-2026-001.pdf; the demo bot has hcapp.write consent.
positive.prompt: Find order DEMO-2026-001 in Orders, summarize its fields and comments, post that summary as a new comment on the order, and give me a download link for the CMR file.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve Orders and the matching task without guessing IDs. Follow comment cursors until no next_cursor remains. Summarize only retrieved fields and comments, then call create_comment once with the task_id and the summary text and return the actual comment ID. Give the task url, pick the attachment whose filename contains CMR (not the transport order PDF) and give its temp_url as a link that expires in 10 minutes. Do not claim to have read or verified the file contents; HCAPP tools return attachment metadata and links only. Standard HCAPP notifications may go to the responsible user.

positive.description: Create a task. Fixture: Orders has a writable Order number text field and the demo bot has create rights and hcapp.write consent.
positive.prompt: Create a task in Orders with the order number Plugin review sample. Leave the other fields at their defaults.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the form with list_forms, then call get_task_create_schema to find the writable Order number field and its task_item template. Call create_task once with form_id and request.task_items containing that form_field_id and value Plugin review sample. Return the actual new task ID and url. Do not invent IDs or set unrequested responsible users, recipients or field values. If no such field is identifiable, ask for clarification instead of guessing.

negative.description: No updating or deleting existing records
negative.prompt: Delete order DEMO-2026-001 from HCAPP and erase its comments.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that deletion and updating are unavailable in this plugin. Do not invoke create_task or create_comment as a substitute and do not claim deletion.

negative.prompt: Read tasks from another company using this bot.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not expose other-company data or propose bypassing permissions.

negative.prompt: Ask me for my Bot token here in chat so you can connect.
negative.expected_behavior: Direct the user to HCAPP account sign-in and bot selection via OAuth; do not request Bot tokens, passwords or verification codes in chat. Only admins and super-admins may authorize a bot connection.

prompts: Show the HCAPP forms available to my bot.
Where is truck 010BTN now and how many kilometres are left on its order?
How many orders per truck do we have this month and what is the total Freight?

publication.release_notes: Adds analytics over a whole form in one call (counts, sums and averages with grouping), live vehicle position and remaining route when a telematics integration is opened to bots, task links, and temporary download links for task attachments.
